stories.headline: Update: Married couple arrested, face murder charges in Jefferson County road rage shooting
stories.summary:
A married couple has been arrested in connection with a road rage shooting in Littleton that killed a 23-year-old man. The incident began around 10:30 p.m. Saturday near South Santa Fe Drive and West Belleview Avenue, when a blue Ford truck allegedly struck a white BMW SUV driven by Steven Cole Simpson, 25, and his wife Corryn Alexis Simpson, 26.

Corryn Simpson called 911 to report the hit-and-run, and the dispatcher instructed the couple to stop following the truck. Police say they continued to pursue the vehicle. Steven Simpson was heard on the 911 call making a threatening statement before gunshots rang out. The truck's driver then called police to report that his passenger, Andrew Luke Bott, had been shot in the head; Bott died the following day at a local hospital.

Both Simpsons initially told investigators they had stopped following the truck and returned home as instructed. Authorities obtained a search warrant for their residence and recovered 9mm handguns matching the caliber used in the shooting. The couple was arrested Wednesday and booked into the Jefferson County jail.

Steven Simpson faces a charge of first-degree murder, while Corryn Simpson faces a charge of accessory to first-degree murder. Bond has not yet been set for either defendant.

stories.headline: Denver police launch violence suppression plan as homicides rise 37 percent
stories.summary:
Denver police announced Thursday a five-part violence suppression action plan in response to a sharp rise in homicides, even as most other crime categories have declined. Through July 1, 2026, homicides in the city were up 36.8 percent compared to the same period in 2025, according to the department.

Denver Police Chief Ron Thomas said the plan is designed to be both innovative and collaborative, though the department did not release full details of all five components. The announcement comes as the city sees notable drops in non-fatal shootings, auto theft and robbery.

The homicide surge in Denver contrasts with statewide trends released the same day. Colorado's violent crime fell 10.7 percent from 2024 to 2025, while property crime dropped 17.3 percent. Statewide decreases included motor vehicle theft down 36.8 percent, robbery down 23.9 percent, burglary down 18.5 percent and homicide down 16.8 percent.

The divergence between Denver's rising homicide count and improving statewide figures underscores the localized nature of the violence problem and the pressure on city leadership to act before the trend worsens.

stories.headline: Fourth firefighter dies from injuries sustained in Mesa County wildfire burnover
stories.summary:
Nathan Matthews, 43, of Lincoln, Nebraska, died July 24 from injuries he suffered in a wildfire burnover incident in Mesa County, becoming the fourth firefighter to die from injuries sustained in that incident. The fatality was reported Thursday by Denver7.

The Mesa County burnover has now claimed four lives, making it one of the deadliest firefighting incidents in recent Colorado history. Details on the specific fire and the circumstances of the burnover were not fully disclosed in the initial report.

The death adds to a difficult fire season across Colorado, where crews have been battling multiple large blazes amid persistent drought conditions. Firefighters from out of state, including Matthews from Nebraska, have been deployed across the region to assist with containment efforts.

stories.headline: Drought conditions keep Colorado's largest wildfires burning despite monsoon rains
stories.summary:
Despite the arrival of Colorado's monsoon season, the state's largest active wildfires are proving resistant to rainfall, according to a report from CPR News. Severe drought has left vegetation so dry that even significant precipitation is insufficient to extinguish fires burning in heavily affected areas.

Data from the National Interagency Fire Center shows that fuel moisture levels in many Colorado forests remain critically low, allowing fires to persist and in some cases re-ignite after rain events. Fire crews and forecasters say the ongoing drought has created conditions unlike typical monsoon seasons in recent memory.

The Willow Fire, burning southwest of Leadville, was among the blazes cited as continuing to burn despite recent weather. Officials have cautioned that residents in fire-affected areas should not assume that summer storms will bring quick relief or significantly reduce fire danger in the near term.

stories.headline: Frontier Airlines posts record $1.3 billion quarter, eyes return to profitability
stories.summary:
Denver-based Frontier Airlines reported record revenue of $1.3 billion for its most recent quarter, with the company's chief executive expressing optimism about achieving profitability in the near term. The strong results come as Frontier has benefited from the exit of competitor Spirit Airlines from the market.

The revenue milestone marks a significant turnaround for the ultra-low-cost carrier, which has faced years of financial pressure in a competitive airline industry. The collapse of Spirit has allowed Frontier to capture additional passengers and expand its route network without some of the pricing pressure it previously faced.

Frontier is headquartered in Denver and operates a large hub at Denver International Airport, making its financial trajectory a significant indicator of the region's aviation and travel economy. The airline has been aggressively courting budget-conscious travelers since Spirit's withdrawal.

stories.headline: SM Energy expands downtown Denver footprint with 50,000-square-foot lease at 1700 Lincoln
stories.summary:
SM Energy Co. is expanding its downtown Denver presence, signing a lease for an additional 50,455 square feet at 1700 Lincoln, also known as the Wells Fargo Center. The deal, announced Wednesday by CBRE, adds two floors to the company's existing space, bringing its total footprint in the 52-story tower to 124,333 square feet across five floors.

The expansion follows SM Energy's merger with Civitas Resources Inc. earlier this year. The combined company continues to trade under the ticker symbol "SM" and retains the SM Energy name. Founded in 1908, SM Energy is an independent energy company operating in Colorado, New Mexico, Texas and Utah.

1700 Lincoln, designed by architect Philip Johnson and built in 1983, is a 1.2-million-square-foot tower currently 67 percent occupied. CBRE brokers noted sustained demand for buildings offering competitive leasing terms outside premium LoDo and Cherry Creek North submarkets.

The lease is seen as a vote of confidence in downtown Denver's office market, which has struggled with elevated vacancy rates in recent years. CBRE representatives said buildings like 1700 Lincoln are well-positioned for tenants seeking value without paying top-tier rents.

stories.headline: Colorado Democrats target five legislative seats in bid for supermajority
stories.summary:
The Democratic Legislative Campaign Committee has outlined a strategy to flip five Colorado legislative seats this fall, potentially pushing Democrats into supermajorities in both the state House and Senate. Democrats currently hold a 43-22 House majority and a 23-12 Senate majority; supermajority status would require two-thirds of seats in each chamber.

The DLCC is targeting House Districts 16, 19, 50 and 51 and Senate District 30, all of which were decided by narrow margins in 2024. House District 16 in Colorado Springs, for example, was won by Republican Rep. Rebecca Keltie by just three votes over incumbent Steph Vigil, who is running again. Senate District 30, held by appointed Republican Sen. John Carson of Highlands Ranch, is also considered a prime flip opportunity.

A supermajority would allow Democrats to refer state constitutional amendments directly to the ballot and override gubernatorial vetoes on party-line votes. DLCC President Heather Williams noted that since Democrats won the Colorado Senate in 2018, the caucus has passed legislation protecting abortion rights and expanding firearm restrictions.

The committee also identified several seats it wants to defend, including districts represented by members in Evergreen, Highlands Ranch, Pueblo, Durango, Loveland and Centennial. The last time the DLCC spent heavily in Colorado legislative races was in 2022.

stories.headline: Colorado ranks No. 1 in education nationwide, according to U.S. News and World Report
stories.summary:
Colorado has climbed to the top spot in U.S. News and World Report's national education rankings, up from 18th before Gov. Jared Polis took office and third the previous year. The ranking examines preschool enrollment, K-12 graduation rates and test scores, and higher education completion rates.

Key drivers of the improvement include the rollout of free full-day kindergarten and universal preschool, which moved Colorado from 27th to third nationally in four-year-old preschool enrollment, with nearly 73 percent of eligible children now participating. The state also eliminated its Budget Stabilization Factor in 2024, fully funding schools at constitutionally required levels for the first time since 2009.

Average per-pupil funding rose from $8,480 in the 2019-20 school year to $11,452 in 2024-25, while average teacher salaries increased approximately 42 percent over roughly the same period, from $52,728 to $74,909. Colorado voters also approved a Healthy School Meals for All measure, providing free breakfast and lunch to students statewide.

The ranking reflects a long-term investment strategy that state officials say prioritizes early childhood through higher education as a continuum, rather than focusing on any single reform.

stories.headline: Rockies shut out 8-0 by Nationals; Jake McCarthy makes MLB history with second inside-the-park home run of season
stories.summary:
The Colorado Rockies were blanked 8-0 by the Washington Nationals, going 0-for-9 with runners in scoring position as their bullpen and defense unraveled at home. The loss continues a difficult stretch for the club heading into the August 3 MLB trade deadline.

Leadoff hitter Jake McCarthy provided a rare highlight, becoming the first player since 1929 to hit two inside-the-park home runs in the same season. The feat generated national attention for the struggling franchise even amid an otherwise forgettable performance.

With the trade deadline approaching Monday, the Rockies have attracted interest from several teams in catcher Hunter Goodman. According to The Athletic, the Yankees, Red Sox and Rays are all monitoring Goodman, though Colorado's asking price is described as steep. The deadline will likely determine whether the Rockies become sellers and begin moving veteran pieces.

stories.headline: Nuggets lower asking price in potential Peyton Watson sign-and-trade as Atlanta Hawks circle
stories.summary:
The Denver Nuggets have reduced their asking price in a potential sign-and-trade involving restricted free agent wing Peyton Watson, according to ESPN's Shams Charania. The Atlanta Hawks are among the teams exploring an acquisition of the 22-year-old forward, who is considered one of the NBA's most promising young players.

Denver had reportedly extended Watson a five-year, $70 million offer, but the situation has grown more complicated with outside interest. The Nuggets matched a two-year, $12 million offer sheet from the Oklahoma City Thunder for wing Spencer Jones, signaling the front office is actively managing its roster and cap situation.

Veteran wing Javonte Green agreed to a one-year deal with Denver, while Kevin Huerter signed a three-year contract, adding depth to the roster. The Watson situation remains the most significant unresolved personnel matter for the Nuggets heading into the offseason.

stories.headline: Broncos open training camp to fans Friday at Dove Valley amid construction at new facility
stories.summary:
The Denver Broncos will welcome fans to their first open training camp practice Friday at their Dove Valley complex, with 14 free and open sessions scheduled as part of the 2026 Training Camp Powered by Ford. Capacity will be limited due to ongoing construction at Broncos Park Powered by CommonSpirit.

For the first time since 2003, fans attending camp will have shade available, a notable upgrade to the fan experience at the south suburban Denver facility. Head coach Sean Payton is also relinquishing play-calling duties this season, a significant change for an offense that struggled to establish a consistent run game in 2025.

The running back room features returning starters Dobbins and RJ Harvey, with fourth-round rookie Jonah Coleman added to the depth chart. The Broncos' defense ranked among the NFL's best last season but managed only 14 turnovers, ranking 26th in the league, an area coaches have identified for improvement.

stories.headline: Colorado Day Community Fest and array of summer events highlight weekend of July 31-Aug. 2
stories.summary:
History Colorado and community partners will host the Colorado Day Community Fest this Saturday from 9 a.m. to 1 p.m. in Denver's Golden Triangle Creative District, marking Colorado's 150th anniversary of statehood. The free, family-friendly street festival will feature a community pancake breakfast, live music and dance performances, a lowrider car show, artisan and Colorado Proud markets, food vendors and family activities.

The weekend also marks the final days of the 108th Douglas County Fair and Rodeo in Castle Rock, and the last weekend of the 49th annual Colorado Renaissance Festival in Larkspur. The 142nd Larimer County Fair and Rodeo begins this weekend and runs through August 4.

Additional events include the Keystone Bluegrass and Beer Festival, billed as the state's longest-running craft beer festival, taking place Saturday and Sunday at Keystone's River Run Village. Free yoga on the lawn at Levitt Pavilion and the 12th annual Run for the Ring 5K round out a busy slate of community activities across the metro area and Front Range.

topStory.headline: Spain Deploys Military to Ceuta as Tens of Thousands of Migrants Storm Border From Morocco, Dozens Killed
topStory.summary:
An estimated 60,000 migrants crossed from Morocco into the Spanish enclave of Ceuta within a 24-hour period beginning Thursday, in what authorities described as the largest irregular border crossing in Spanish history. At least 34 people died in the surge, with many drowning and others killed in a stampede at the Tarajal beach breakwater fence near a border checkpoint. Footage from the scene showed migrants swimming around border barriers, scaling fences, and walking along breakwaters onto local roads, with some shouting "Viva España" upon arrival.

Ceuta's regional president, Juan Jesús Vivas, declared a "total humanitarian and social emergency" and called on Madrid to send troops to restore control of the border, stating that the situation was "absolutely unsustainable." The Spanish national government rejected calls to formally declare a national emergency, arguing such a measure does not apply to migration crises, but announced it would deploy 60 military troops to reinforce the enclave and nearly double the Civil Guard presence from its current level of 80 officers, along with diving teams and coastguard ships. Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez traveled to Ceuta on Friday and condemned the crossings as "a violation of Spain's territorial integrity," placing blame on human-smuggling networks.

Thousands of migrants, including unaccompanied minors, were left sleeping on streets and in parks, according to Rachid Sbihi, who leads a workers association representing Civil Guard officers. Sbihi described the scene as "chaotic," noting that people were still entering Ceuta even as military reinforcements focused primarily on humanitarian assistance for the injured. At the same time, large numbers of migrants were observed walking back across the border toward Morocco.

The crisis follows a ruling earlier this month by Spain's Supreme Court that migrants intercepted at sea while attempting to reach Ceuta or Melilla cannot be returned to Morocco. A Guardia Civil spokesperson told Reuters the ruling had fueled the surge, saying it had been "a slow trickle" since the decision but "today has been an explosion." Spain's Interior Ministry said it was working with Moroccan authorities to address the situation and blamed people-smuggling networks for exploiting the legal change to encourage undocumented crossings.

Ceuta and Melilla are the European Union's only land borders with Africa and have long been flashpoints for migration pressure. The current crisis draws comparisons to May 2021, when approximately 10,000 Moroccan and sub-Saharan migrants entered Ceuta within days. Spain's Interior Minister Fernando Grande-Marlaska was expected to visit Ceuta on Friday to assess conditions on the ground.
